assertion: Based on results so far, an estimated 75% of Michigan's rivers and streams likely exceed state limits for fecal contamination, said Molly Rippke, who leads E. coli testing for the Michigan Department of Environment, Great Lakes and Energy.
measure: Michigan river E. coli water quality samples
warehouse_value: WQP Michigan 2021-2025: 1,172 of 1,493 E. coli sites (78%) had a sample over 300/100mL; 821 (55%) over 1,000
sql: SELECT COUNT(*), SUM(CASE WHEN mx>300 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) FROM (SELECT monitoring_location_id, MAX(result_value) mx FROM environment.water_quality_samples WHERE state='26' AND "year" BETWEEN 2021 AND 2025 AND characteristic_name='Escherichia coli' GROUP BY monitoring_location_id) t
reason: Preliminary agency estimate, reported faithfully; EGLE's own page still says roughly half.
independent_value: EGLE standards page; Michigan Public republication carries same estimate

assertion: The vast majority exceeded levels deemed safe for swimming. In more than half, levels are often too high even for even partial body contact activities, like paddling or wading.
warehouse_value: 78% of sites any sample >300; 55% any sample >1,000
reason: Warehouse proxy (single samples, non-random sites) is consistent with the claim.

assertion: Full-body swimming: No more than 300 E. coli at any given time, and a mean of no more than 130 E. coli across multiple samples during a 30-day period; Partial-body contact: No more than 1,000 E. coli at any given time
independent_value: EGLE: 300 and 1,000 are daily maximum geometric means, 130 a 30-day geometric mean, swimming limits May 1 to Oct 31
inaccuracy: The article says 'at any given time'; EGLE defines the 300 and 1,000 limits as geometric means and applies swimming limits only May 1 to Oct 31.

sql: SELECT SUBSTR(geo_name, POSITION(', ' IN geo_name)+2) st, SUM(population) pop FROM census.pep_population WHERE "year"=2023 AND geography='county' GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY pop DESC

assertion: estimates from the US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention suggest the nationwide toll could top a million.
independent_value: CDC EID 29(7): 5.61 million recreational-water illnesses (95% CrI 2.97-9.00M), 7.15 million total waterborne, 2014
inaccuracy: The source estimates 5.61 million recreational-water illnesses (mostly ear infections), far above 'a million'; 1.13 million is the drinking-water figure.

assertion: One Michigan-based study found waterborne E. coli outbreaks diminished home prices by an average of $13,000 when a sale coincided with an outbreak.
independent_value: Cambridge study: proximity to E. coli outbreaks leads to an 8.9% price drop for houses sold during outbreaks, over $13,000 for the average house; effects do not persist

assertion: If lakes are the heart of Michigan, its 76,000 miles of rivers and streams are its arteries and pulse
independent_value: Bridge's septic story also states 76,000 miles; not confirmed on an agency page here

assertion: In Indiana, 74% of assessed river miles exceed regulatory limits. In Illinois, the figure is 83%.
measure: Indiana Illinois assessed river miles impaired recreation bacteria
reason: Warehouse has no state assessment tables; searches of IDEM/EPA documents did not surface the figures.
